ths.text: Akros was founded by Elektes and six warriors, inspired by Iroas, after the war between humans and minotaurs. Its prince Anax lives under a father who shows contempt for him, as King Athanas looks proudly at Timoteus and coldly at Anax in front of the soldiers.

Anax trains with Zotikos and then with the advisor Kaletor, a former pankration competitor, and at the Iroan Games he baits Timoteus into the kneebar that crippled Kaletor and wins by reversing it. He then rebukes Timoteus for trying to cripple him, which wins the crowd's respect, and Timoteus is publicly whipped for treason.

Later Xenagos besieges Akros with minotaurs, and Cymede offers herself to Keranos, who turns the Deyda River into an elemental that consumes them. Rhordon, aided by Mogis, impales King Anax, but Elspeth saves him, and Xenagos uses the victory celebration to stage the Great Revel and ascend to godhood, after which Anax dies and Cymede is missing, and their niece Taranika becomes regent.

bng.text: Mogis sends minotaur hordes against human cities, and Akros bears the brunt, with the walls of the city besieged by a wall the minotaurs themselves have built. Elspeth leads an army of heroes from Akros, Meletis and Setessa to break the siege.
Yet the victory celebration becomes the ritual that launches Xenagos into Nyx as a god, and Elspeth is blamed and driven away.

jou.text: At the Akroan gates, hoplites revive the tactics of Kytheon Iora's irregulars, and Elspeth and Daxos travel to Akros, where Xenagos tells her how to destroy the army by raising the river. The Akroans defeat Mogis's minotaur horde and celebrate, but Xenagos uses the occasion for his final ritual of ascension to godhood, and under his control Elspeth kills Daxos.

thb.text: Akros is saved when Keranos, circumventing the Silence of the Gods, sends prophetic visions to Queen Cymede, helping her destroy the minotaur army of Rhordon with a steam elemental. King Anax fights Rhordon, who is aided by Mogis, and is impaled, but Elspeth saves him and Rhordon is washed away by Keranos's river elemental.
As a reward for her faith, Keranos takes Cymede from Akros shortly before the Great Revel, and Anax dies within two years, possibly of his injuries, so that Taranika serves as regent of Akros.
In another story from the city, Pavios moves to Akros, meets Thanasis, and they fall in love, but their fathers forbid the meetings, and Pavios finds Thanasis dead against the emonberry tree.
